Foreign residents should study katakana words so that they can read official documents.
items.explanation: The writer criticizes the overuse of katakana words and concludes that the key is choosing words from the reader's standpoint. B is explicitly rejected (すべてのカタカナ語を排除せよと言うつもりはない). C overstates the one advantage the writer grants. D reverses the argument: documents should be readable by everyone, including foreigners.

items.stem: According to the writer, what is a less obvious problem with katakana words?
choices: They are harder for older readers to type and to look up in dictionaries.
Writers often use them without being clear about the meaning themselves.
They make official documents much longer than the plain Japanese versions.
They were banned by a government rule that officials continue to ignore.
items.explanation: The third paragraph says the problem is not only that the words are hard to understand but that 書き手自身も意味をあいまいにしたまま使っている. Typing (A), length (C) and a ban (D) are not mentioned; in fact the plain Japanese version at the end is about as long.

items.stem: Which best describes the writer's attitude toward katakana words?
choices: Enthusiastic, seeing them as a sign of modern, international government.
Indifferent, regarding the issue as unimportant.
Hostile, demanding that they all be replaced immediately.
Critical of their overuse, but accepting of established loanwords.
items.explanation: The writer criticizes unclear overuse yet says forcing replacements for already established words would sound unnatural. That is a moderate, critical stance. A and B do not match the column's clear criticism, and C is contradicted by the final paragraph.

items.stem: What is the writer's main position?
choices: Smartphones cause no real problems in class, so the board should not make any rules.
Some rules are needed, but flexible rules would be better than a total ban.
The ban does not go far enough and should cover the whole school day, including breaks.
Students themselves should decide whether to use smartphones, without any school rules.
items.explanation: The editorial accepts that harm from overuse has some basis and that rules are needed, but questions a total ban and asks for flexible, class-by-class rules. A contradicts the acceptance of the harm; C goes in the opposite direction; D ignores the call for rules decided with teachers and students.

items.stem: Which student does the writer say could be especially disadvantaged by the ban?
choices: A student who cannot take a school device home.
A student who has been a victim of online bullying through social media.
A student who does not own a smartphone of his or her own.
A student who is preparing for university entrance exams.
items.explanation: The writer mentions students who, 家庭の事情で (because of family circumstances), cannot take school devices home and for whom their own smartphone may be the only learning tool. The other students are not given as examples; bullying is mentioned only as one of the board's reasons for the ban.

items.stem: Which best describes the tone of the editorial?
choices: Angry and mocking toward the board of education.
Fully supportive of the board's decision.
Neutral, simply reporting the decision without comment.
Understanding of the concern but critical of the chosen measure.
items.explanation: The writer says the judgment that rules are needed is understandable (理解できる) but doubts that a total ban is best, and makes a polite request (検討してほしい). That is measured criticism, not anger (A), support (B) or neutrality (C).

items.stem: What is the main point of the article?
choices: The record turnout shows that residents' complaints about the base have been exaggerated.
A record turnout exposed traffic problems, raising how to balance the event with residents' lives.
After the complaints, the city has asked the base to cancel next year's air festival.
The city and the chamber of commerce have agreed to adopt an advance reservation system for next year's event.
items.explanation: The article pairs the record 「約4万2千人」 with 「課題も浮かび上がった」 and ends on how to adjust three positions (「どう調整するか、関係者の議論はこれからだ」). No one calls the complaints exaggerated or asks for cancellation, and the reservation system is only being considered, with the chamber voicing concern.

items.stem: What is the city official's stance?
choices: The festival matters economically, but crowd growth should not be the only goal.
The festival should be moved to a site far from any residential district.
The base alone is responsible for solving the parking and traffic problems.
A reservation system should be opposed because it would reduce local sales.
items.explanation: The official 「大きな意味を持つことは認めつつも」 says the aim should not be 「来場者数を増やすことだけ」 but coexistence with residents, to be worked out 「基地と一緒に」 — so not the base alone. Moving the site is never proposed, and the sales worry comes from the chamber, not the city.

items.stem: Why is the chamber of commerce wary of a reservation system?
choices: Its members would have to manage the reservations themselves.
The booths were new this year and have not yet made a profit.
It would be responsible for running the temporary parking lots.
Fewer visitors would mean lower sales at the food booths.
items.explanation: The chamber's worry is 「予約制によって来場者が減れば売り上げに響く」. The article does not say it would handle reservations or parking, and although the booths were new (「初めて設けた」), profitability is not mentioned.

items.stem: Which issue remained unresolved at the end of the meeting?
choices: Early-morning flights, which the base refused to limit in any way
The route over the southern district, which the base would not alter
Whether to meet again, since the two sides failed to reach agreement
Evening flights, whose timing the base said it could not change for now
items.explanation: Residents noted 「夕方の飛行についての言及がない」 and the base replied 「時間帯を変えることは難しい」. Early flights before 7 a.m. and the southern route were both addressed by the base's two measures, and the sides 「協議を続けることでは合意した」.

items.stem: What does 「持ち帰って検討する」 tell us about the base's response to the deputy mayor?
choices: It accepted the request and will start the system right away.
It politely but firmly rejected the request as outside its own authority.
It made no commitment then, but will consider the request internally.
It asked the town to design the notification system itself.
items.explanation: 「持ち帰って検討する」 means taking a matter back to one's organization to consider — neither an on-the-spot yes nor a refusal. Nothing in the minutes shifts the work of designing the system onto the town.

items.stem: What is planned for the next meeting?
choices: Presenting a new schedule for the evening training flights
Checking the new route's effect against noise measurement data
Having residents vote on whether to keep the new route
Reporting on complaints from the southern district only
items.explanation: Section 4 says 「新しい経路の効果を騒音測定の結果とともに確認する」. No evening schedule, vote or southern-only report is planned; the southern district is only where complaints concentrated.

items.stem: According to Takano, what matters most in a liaison officer's work?
choices: Understanding how the partner organization makes its decisions
Translating every word of the other side's messages precisely
Having the authority to make decisions on the spot for both
Building close personal friendships with U.S. commanders
items.explanation: She says language skill is needed but 「それ以上に大切なのは、相手の組織がどのようなプロセスで動くかを知っていること」, and adds that word-for-word translation alone causes trouble. She never claims decision authority or stresses personal friendships.

items.stem: Why can 「明日の朝までに決めます」 cause a misunderstanding?
choices: The two forces place decision authority at different levels, so it weighs differently.
U.S. officers are unfamiliar with the way Japanese speakers express deadlines and times.
SDF commanders tend to forget such promises once the exercise is underway.
The phrase sounds too casual and therefore impolite to a senior officer.
items.explanation: She explains that U.S. field commanders decide much themselves while the SDF waits for 「上級部隊の承認」, so the same promise 「意味する重みが違う」; misunderstandings come from 「組織の構造の違い」, not language or forgetfulness or politeness.

items.stem: What does her answer about when she feels rewarded suggest?
choices: She is frustrated that her work so rarely receives any recognition.
She prefers quiet days on which there is no liaison work to do at all.
She sees problems as the best chance to show others what liaison work can really do.
She treats a lack of trouble as the sign that unseen coordination worked.
items.explanation: She says 「問題が起きなかったということは、誰かがどこかで調整をしていたということ」 and, far from resenting being unnoticed, says 「信頼の土台はそこにあると思っています」. That rules out frustration; quiet days are the result of work, not an absence of it; and she values problems not arising, not problems themselves.

items.stem: What is the main point of the article?
choices: Kitahama has switched all of its suburban routes to self-driving buses to solve its driver shortage.
Kitahama has begun a self-driving bus trial that raises hopes but still faces unresolved problems.
Elderly residents of Kitahama have complained that the self-driving bus drives roughly.
Kitahama has already decided to introduce self-driving buses permanently next spring.
items.explanation: The article reports the start of a limited trial (weekday daytime, six runs a day) that is hoped to help with the driver shortage, then sets out the problems: staff costs, winter sensors and an undecided future. A is wrong: it is a trial on one suburban route, and the city says the buses will not replace drivers soon. C is wrong: the woman quoted said the driving was more careful than she expected. D is wrong: the city will decide on full introduction only after the trial ends in March.

items.stem: According to the professor, why will personnel costs hardly fall for now?
choices: Because the buses run only six times a day.
Because the sensors are expensive to maintain.
Because a staff member still has to ride on every bus.
Because too few passengers use the service.
items.explanation: The professor says 係員が乗っている限り、人件費はほとんど減らない: as long as an attendant rides along, labor costs barely fall; the real turning point is running without staff. The number of runs, sensor costs and passenger numbers are not what he gives as the reason.

items.stem: What can be inferred about the city's position on winter operation?
choices: It plans to cancel the whole trial as soon as snow begins to fall this winter.
It has confirmed through tests that the sensors work reliably on snowy roads.
It has asked residents to vote on whether the buses should keep running in winter.
It has not decided yet, since snow may affect the sensors.
items.explanation: The city 結論を先送りした (postponed a decision) on winter operation because the sensors may not read the road surface correctly in snow. That implies uncertainty, not a decision. A overstates it (nothing says the trial will be cancelled), B contradicts the stated risk, and no vote of residents is mentioned (C).

items.stem: What is the main point of the report?
choices: They agreed on a military hotline to avoid accidental clashes, but the core dispute remains.
They settled the territorial dispute and agreed to set up a hotline to manage the waters jointly.
The talks broke down because the two sides could not agree on the wording of the joint statement.
The two countries agreed to hold joint naval exercises in the disputed waters to build trust.
items.explanation: The report centers on the hotline agreement and notes that the fundamental territorial conflict 解消されなかった (was not resolved), so B is wrong. C is wrong: a joint statement was issued, even though drafting continued until just before the talks. D (joint exercises) is not mentioned.

items.stem: What does the joint statement's silence about the disputed waters suggest?
choices: The dispute is no longer regarded as important by either side.
The two countries now plan to share the waters equally.
The two sides still disagree sharply on the issue.
A neutral country will now administer the waters.
items.explanation: The article says the omission 両国の立場の隔たりの大きさをうかがわせた: it suggested how far apart the two positions are. A is wrong because the dispute caused rising tension; B and D are not mentioned anywhere. The neutral country only hosted the summit.

items.stem: Experts call the agreement 「最低限の安全装置」. What does this expression mean here?
choices: a complete solution to the territorial dispute
a basic safeguard that lowers the danger of escalation
a new weapons system to defend the disputed waters
a temporary measure that experts oppose
items.explanation: 最低限 means 'minimum' and 安全装置 'safety device'. The researcher explains that the hotline does not solve the problem itself but lowers the risk that a misunderstanding leads to armed conflict, so it is a minimal safeguard. A contradicts 'does not solve the problem itself'; C takes 装置 too literally; D is wrong because experts evaluate it positively (評価する声が多い).

items.stem: What is the article mainly about?
choices: A new local festival that promotes saury as the traditional taste of autumn in Tohoku.
How overfishing by foreign boats has reduced saury catches off the Tohoku coast.
A government plan to move Tohoku fishers to ports in western Japan where fish are plentiful.
How warmer seas changed a port's catch and how fishers are responding.
items.explanation: The article links the fall in saury and the arrival of warm-water fish to rising water temperatures, then describes the fishers' different responses. A, B and C are not mentioned; the only cause discussed is the temperature change.

items.stem: According to the fisheries station, how much have nearby sea temperatures risen?
choices: About 1.5 degrees on average over thirty years.
About 1.5 degrees in the last five years.
About 3 degrees over thirty years.
About 7 degrees since saury catches began to fall.
items.explanation: The station says 近海の水温はこの三十年で平均一・五度ほど上がった: an average rise of about 1.5 degrees over thirty years. Five years is the period of the saury decline, and seven (七割) refers to the 70 percent fall in the catch, not degrees.

items.stem: In the third paragraph, 加工品の開発に乗り出した means that some cooperatives have...
choices: given up developing processed products because sales were poor.
been ordered by the government to develop processed products.
started actively working on developing processed products.
sailed out to sea to look for new kinds of fish for processing.
items.explanation: 乗り出す here means to set about or launch into an undertaking. The following sentence confirms the result: canned yellowtail is already selling well. A is the opposite, nothing says anyone ordered it (B), and D takes the literal 'set out to sea' meaning, which does not fit with 開発に.

items.stem: What does the agreement restrict, in principle?
choices: All flight training on weekends.
The extension of the runway.
The number of aircraft stationed at the base.
Flight training between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
items.explanation: The agreement says night flight training will, in principle (原則として), not be carried out from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Weekends, the runway and the number of aircraft are not restricted by it; the runway extension is mentioned only as the cause of more training.

items.stem: What caused complaints to rise sharply three years ago?
choices: The amount of training increased after the runway was extended.
The base began flying at night for the first time.
The towns stopped paying for soundproofing work.
A new type of aircraft arrived at the base.
items.explanation: Complaints rose from three years ago, when training increased as the runway was extended (滑走路の延長に伴って訓練の回数が増えた). Nothing says night flights were new, that soundproofing subsidies stopped (the agreement expands them), or that new aircraft arrived.

items.stem: Why does one residents' group want the number of exceptions published every month?
choices: They want the base to be able to fly more often when emergency missions arise.
They believe the agreement already bans every night flight, with no exceptions at all.
They doubt the exceptions will be kept narrow and want to check.
They want to compare the base's record with that of other bases around the country.
items.explanation: The group says the scope of the exceptions is vague and it is unclear how far the rule will be kept, and asks for monthly figures to increase transparency. That shows distrust and a wish to monitor. A is the opposite; B ignores the exception clause the group complains about; D is not mentioned.

items.stem: What is the main finding of the report?
choices: Evacuation shelters could not be opened in time, although casualty transport went smoothly.
Most tasks went to plan, but information sharing among organizations was weak.
The drill was too large to manage, so the prefecture should hold smaller drills in the future.
The communication lines worked without trouble, but the organizations used too many radios.
items.explanation: The report says shelters and casualty transport went roughly to plan, while information sharing between organizations left a major problem (大きな課題). A contradicts the statement that shelters opened as planned. C is never suggested; the drill is valued precisely because it revealed failures. D contradicts the report: lines became congested and headquarters lost track of the situation for a time.

items.stem: What does the prefecture plan to do by next fiscal year?
choices: Double the number of organizations taking part in the drill.
Build new evacuation shelters along the coast.
Give every organization its own separate radio system.
Introduce a common information system shared by the organizations.
items.explanation: The crisis management section 来年度までに共通の情報システムを導入する方針を示した: it will introduce a common information system by next fiscal year. C is the opposite: separate radios were the cause of the delays. A and B are not mentioned.

items.stem: Why does the report say that finding failures was itself an achievement?
choices: Because the failures showed that the organizations did not need any further training.
Because the prefecture was required by law to report at least one failure after each drill.
Because the failures could be blamed on the other organizations rather than on the prefecture.
Because problems found in a drill can be fixed before a real disaster.
items.explanation: The last paragraph links the remark to 本番で同じ失敗を繰り返さないために: the point of a drill is to find problems so they are not repeated in a real disaster. Nothing suggests less training is needed (A), a legal reporting requirement (B), or shifting blame to others (C).

items.stem: What is the main point of the article?
choices: Young people have stopped reading altogether, whether on paper or on screens.
Paper books have become more popular than e-books among young people over ten years.
Fewer read paper books and more read on screens, but many give up on long texts.
Libraries plan to replace paper books with tablets because young people prefer screens.
items.explanation: The survey shows fewer paper-book readers, more screen reading, and a worrying tendency to give up on long texts. A is contradicted by the screen-reading figures and the institute's comment. B is the opposite of the data. D is not mentioned; libraries are only said to face a challenge.

items.stem: What share of respondents said they read texts on a screen for three hours or more a week?
choices: About 15 percent
More than 60 percent
Just over half (52 percent)
Exactly half of them
items.explanation: The article says 六割を超えた: over 60 percent. 52 percent is the share who read no paper book in the past month, and 15 points is the increase in that figure over ten years; 'exactly half' is not given.

items.stem: What does the institute's staff member suggest?
choices: Schools should ban reading on screens and return to paper books to protect concentration.
Reading on screens is better because it lets young people read more text every week.
Being able to read with focus to the end matters more than the medium.
Young people should read fewer long articles and more short texts that suit screens.
items.explanation: The staff member says one should not think in terms of paper versus screen; what matters is gaining the experience of reading to the end with concentration in any medium. A and B each take one side of the paper-versus-screen contrast the speaker rejects. D reverses the point: the concern is that people give up on long texts, not that they should read shorter ones.

items.stem: What is the writer's main point?
choices: Machine translation is still too inaccurate to be trusted for business e-mails with foreign partners.
People should stop using translation apps so that they are forced to learn foreign languages.
Learning languages is no longer worth the time, now that translation apps are good enough.
Translation handles information, but learning a language still brings nuance and new perspectives.
items.explanation: The writer grants that translation is sufficient for passing on information but argues that nuance and new ways of dividing up the world come only from learning a language, so its meaning moves beyond usefulness. A contradicts the first paragraph; B contradicts 使わない手はない (it would be foolish not to use it); C is the view the writer partly concedes but ultimately rejects.

items.stem: What does the writer mean by 一理はある at the start of the second paragraph?
choices: The question is completely wrong.
The question has some validity.
The question has only one correct answer.
The question is too difficult to answer.
items.explanation: 一理ある means 'there is some truth or reason in it'. The writer then explains in what limited sense the question is reasonable (for information and business purposes) before pointing out what it overlooks. A is the opposite; C and D misread 一理 as 'one answer' or as a comment on difficulty.

items.stem: What does the example of 「よろしくお願いします」 illustrate?
choices: Translation apps are unable to translate Japanese greetings into English at all.
Japanese has far fewer polite expressions than English, so they are hard to translate.
A translation can give the surface meaning but miss the nuances.
Learners should memorize set phrases like this one before they start studying grammar.
items.explanation: The writer says an app will produce plausible English, but the implications (expectations for the relationship, a stance of leaving things to the other person) are hard to feel from the translation. A is contradicted: the app does produce a translation. B and D are not claimed.

items.stem: Which best describes the tone of the column?
choices: Reflective and measured, valuing the tool while questioning a narrow view of language.
Hostile toward new technology and nostalgic for a time when people learned languages the hard way.
Excited and promotional, recommending a particular translation app to readers who travel.
Sarcastic and dismissive toward people who still spend years studying foreign languages.
items.explanation: The writer concedes 一理はある, says machine translation is a useful tool that one would be foolish not to use (使わない手はない), and closes with a tentative question (のではないだろうか). That is thoughtful and balanced. B is wrong because the writer endorses the tool; C because no product is promoted; D because the column defends language learning.

items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?
choices: The grants have succeeded in reversing the flow of people from the regions into big cities.
Municipalities waste grant money because many of their officials are dishonest or careless.
The state should specify in detail which projects each municipality carries out with the money.
The grant system bred copycat, number-driven projects; towns need room to experiment.
items.explanation: The commentary blames the grant structure (projects fitted to the state's framework, success measured by numbers) and concludes that the state should widen municipalities' room for trial and error. A contradicts the first paragraph (the trend has not changed); B is never claimed, since the writer says choosing approvable projects is rational; C is the opposite of the conclusion.

items.stem: In the third paragraph, the writer says the system 形骸化していった. What does this mean?
choices: It grew stronger and more effective.
It became an empty formality that had lost its real substance.
It was abolished by law.
It was taken over by private companies.
items.explanation: 形骸化 (from 形骸, a shell or skeleton) means that something keeps its outward form but loses its substance. The context supports this: making plans and reports became a yearly ritual while the real question of whether life improved was left behind. The other options are not described in the text.

items.stem: According to the writer, what do the regions that achieved results have in common?
choices: Residents already knew what they wanted to protect and change.
They received larger grants than other regions because their plans were well written.
They used the grants to build large tourist facilities that attract visitors.
They are located close enough to big cities for people to commute.
items.explanation: The fourth paragraph says what they share is that residents had their own question (何を守り、何を変えたいのか) before the state's system, with money only as support. Grant size and location are not mentioned, and tourist facilities are cited as examples of copycat projects (C).

items.stem: Why, according to the writer, do so many municipalities end up with similar projects?
choices: Residents demand the same kinds of facilities that they have seen in other towns.
The law requires every municipality to build at least one tourist facility.
The system makes it rational to pick projects likely to be approved.
Officials know little about their own regions and copy what others have done.
items.explanation: The second paragraph says that because grants go to projects matching the state's framework, it becomes more rational (合理的) for municipalities to pick projects likely to be adopted than to design their own, and the result is uniform projects. The writer blames the system's incentives, not officials' ignorance (D); residents' demands (A) and a legal requirement (B) are not mentioned.

items.stem: What is the editorial's central argument?
choices: Spending should be cut, because tension in the region has eased and deterrence is already strong enough.
The government should explain the purpose, content and funding before fixing the total.
Every detail of the new equipment should be made public at once so that citizens can judge it.
The increase is acceptable as long as it is funded by borrowing rather than by higher taxes.
items.explanation: The writer accepts that the security environment is harsher but objects to deciding the total before showing what it is for, asks for an explanation Parliament can verify, and demands an answer on funding. A contradicts the first paragraph, which acknowledges rising tension. C is rejected: the writer concedes that some details must stay secret. D is wrong: the writer asks who will bear the burden if borrowing is used and does not endorse it.

items.stem: In the second paragraph, the writer calls the situation 本末転倒. What does this mean here?
choices: a sudden reversal of government policy under outside pressure
an unavoidable result of the rising tension in the region
putting the secondary matter ahead of the essential one
a small mistake in the budget that can easily be corrected later
items.explanation: 本末転倒 means confusing the root (本) with the branches (末), i.e. putting the less important thing first. Here the total amount, which should follow from a plan, is fixed before the plan itself is shown. It does not mean a policy reversal (A); the writer does not treat it as unavoidable (B) or as trivial (D).

items.stem: What does the writer imply about the government's claim that details must stay secret?
choices: Some secrecy is justified, but not about why the equipment is needed and what it will achieve.
It is entirely false, since in a democracy no defense information should ever be kept from citizens.
It shows that the government has no real plan and is hiding that fact behind secrecy.
It means Parliament should leave defense matters to experts and stop debating the details.
items.explanation: The writer concedes 確かに that full disclosure would reveal one's hand, but distinguishes information that must be secret from information citizens need, such as the reasons and expected effects. B ignores that concession; C goes beyond what the text says; D contradicts the call for Parliament to verify the spending.

items.stem: What is the main point of the editorial?
choices: Rigid rule-following and fear of false alarms delayed evacuation; officials need more discretion.
The rainfall could not have been predicted, so the officials who followed the manual cannot be blamed.
Manuals should be abolished and evacuation decisions left to residents' own experience.
The main cause of the damage was that the river embankments had been built too low.
items.explanation: The editorial argues that treating the manual's thresholds as a reason not to act, together with fear of false alarms, delayed the order, and it calls for discretion for officials. B ignores the criticism of the officials' response; C is wrong because the writer values manuals and says residents' rules of thumb are no longer reliable; D (embankments) is not discussed.

items.stem: In the third paragraph, what does 空振り mean?
choices: an evacuation order that is issued too late to help
a flood that turns out to be larger than anyone expected
an order issued when nothing ends up happening
a manual that has not been updated for many years
items.explanation: 空振り literally means swinging and missing. The text defines it in context: 避難指示を出しても何も起きなければ, an evacuation order after which nothing happens. It is contrasted with 見逃し (missing a real danger). A describes 見逃し-type failures, not 空振り; B and D do not fit.

items.stem: The writer says leaders should 肝に銘じる their duty. What does this mean?
choices: to hand the duty over to others
to take it to heart and keep it firmly in mind
to question whether the duty really exists
to announce it publicly at a press conference
items.explanation: 肝に銘じる (literally to engrave on one's liver) means to take something to heart and never forget it. The sentence urges leaders to remember firmly that they must decide without fearing false alarms. The other meanings do not match the idiom.

items.stem: What does the writer suggest about residents who rely on 'it has always been fine before'?
choices: Their experience is no longer a reliable guide because the climate is changing.
They are right, because most evacuation orders turn out to be false alarms.
They should be punished for not evacuating.
Their experience should be written into the new manual.
items.explanation: The fourth paragraph says this rule of thumb もはや当てにならない (can no longer be relied on) now that the climate is changing. B contradicts the writer's argument; C and D are not proposed.

items.stem: What is the main point of the editorial?
choices: The summit was a historic success that has finally ended the dispute over the border.
Vague wording enabled agreement, but concrete follow-up is needed soon.
The leaders should never have met, because their positions were too far apart to bridge.
The joint statement set a clear timetable for reducing troops near the border.
items.explanation: The editorial grants that ambiguity made agreement possible but warns that without concrete working-level schedules and goals the statement may become a dead letter (空文化). A repeats the governments' claim that the writer doubts; C is never suggested, since the writer values continuing dialogue; D is contradicted: neither the scale nor the timing of reductions was given.

items.stem: What does 玉虫色 describe in this editorial?
choices: bright and cheerful, meant to create a friendly mood at the summit
strongly worded and threatening toward the other side
deliberately ambiguous, so each side can read it its own way
kept secret from the public until the talks are finished
items.explanation: 玉虫色 (the shifting color of a jewel beetle) describes wording that looks different depending on the angle, i.e. deliberately ambiguous. The text explains that such wording lets both sides tell their public they 'won'. The other options miss this idiomatic sense; the statement was published, so D is also factually wrong.

items.stem: Why does the writer say that ambiguity has diplomatic value?
choices: It allows officials to finish writing the statement more quickly before the deadline.
It keeps the details of the agreement hidden from third countries in the region.
It makes further working-level negotiations unnecessary for both governments.
It lets both leaders claim success at home without written concessions.
items.explanation: The third paragraph explains that both leaders face hard-line domestic opinion, so written concessions would be politically costly, and vague wording lets each side say it won. A and B are not mentioned, and C is the opposite of the writer's call for working-level talks.

items.stem: Which best describes the writer's attitude toward the outcome of the summit?
choices: Cautiously skeptical: it sees some value, but real progress is not yet shown.
Enthusiastic, echoing the governments' claim that the summit was a historic step forward.
Completely dismissive, calling the talks a waste of time for both governments.
Neutral, describing the statement's contents without offering any evaluation of them.
items.explanation: The writer says the result is hard to welcome unreservedly (手放しで喜べる内容とは言いがたい) yet acknowledges the diplomatic use of ambiguity and calls it a kind of wisdom for keeping dialogue alive. That is guarded skepticism. B contradicts the doubts, C ignores the acknowledged value, and D ignores the clear evaluation and recommendations.

items.stem: What is the editorial's main point?
choices: The bill should be passed quickly because attacks on infrastructure are an urgent threat.
The country does not need cyber defense measures, since attacks cause only limited damage.
Private companies, not the government, should be responsible for defending infrastructure.
Some defense is needed, but the bill's standards and oversight are too vague to rush.
items.explanation: The editorial accepts the threat and the need for preparation, then raises unclear criteria, monitoring and a vague committee, and warns parliament not to hurry. A is the approach the writer warns against; B contradicts both 被害は計り知れない and 何らかの備えは必要である; C is not discussed.

items.stem: What problem does the writer raise about identifying attackers?
choices: Attacks are often routed through third-country servers, hiding the true source.
Attackers always use the same server, which makes it easy to block them but hard to punish them.
The government refuses to share data on attacks with other countries, including its allies.
Identifying attackers would require reading the content of every message sent in the country.
items.explanation: The second paragraph says attackers often use third-country servers as stepping stones (踏み台), making it hard to identify the source, and a wrong judgment could cause a diplomatic problem. B contradicts this; C is not mentioned; D is not claimed: content monitoring comes up only as a privacy concern.

items.stem: The editorial ends with あらかじめ釘を刺しておきたい. What does 釘を刺す mean here?
choices: to praise something in advance
to warn firmly in advance so that something is not neglected
to postpone a decision
to criticize something after it has happened
items.explanation: 釘を刺す (literally to drive in a nail) means to give a firm reminder or warning beforehand. With あらかじめ (in advance), the writer is warning parliament now that standards and oversight must be written into the law. It is not praise (A), postponement (C) or after-the-fact criticism (D).

items.stem: What does the writer fear about the independent committee?
choices: It will be so strict and slow that it blocks nearly every operation the government proposes.
It will come under the influence of foreign governments through its members.
With vague rules on its members and powers, it may just rubber-stamp government decisions.
It will be too expensive to run and will need a large permanent staff.
items.explanation: The fourth paragraph notes that membership, powers and approval standards are barely specified, raising the concern that the committee will merely ratify (追認する) government judgments. The fear is that it will be too weak, not too strict (A); B and D are not mentioned.

items.stem: What is the writer's main conclusion?
choices: A country can only be safe if it has more and better weapons than all of its rivals.
Alliances should be avoided, because they only create fears of entrapment and abandonment.
Stable deterrence depends mostly on ways to avoid misreading each other's intentions.
Deterrence no longer works in the modern world, so countries should give up military preparations.
items.explanation: The final paragraph says the key to stable deterrence lies less in the balance of power than in mechanisms that prevent misreading intentions, with dialogue alongside military preparation. A is undermined by the security dilemma described in the second paragraph. B overstates the point about alliances, which the writer says also raise deterrence. D is never argued; the writer wants deterrence to be sustainable.

items.stem: What does the writer mean by the 'security dilemma'?
choices: A country cannot decide whether joining an alliance will make it safer or more exposed.
Weapons become outdated faster than a country can afford to replace them with new ones.
Governments cannot agree on how much of the national budget should be spent on defense.
Arming for self-defense leads the other side to arm too, leaving both less secure.
items.explanation: The second paragraph explains it: strengthening arms to protect oneself is seen as a threat, the other side arms as well, and both end up with more weapons yet less security. A refers to the alliance discussion, which is a different point; B and C are not mentioned.

items.stem: According to the essay, what two fears can an alliance create?
choices: Fear of being drawn into an ally's conflict and fear of being abandoned by the ally.
Fear of higher taxes and fear of losing trade.
Fear of spies and fear of cyberattacks.
Fear that the ally will become too weak and fear that it will change its government.
items.explanation: The fourth paragraph names 巻き込まれ (entrapment, being dragged into an ally's conflict) and 見捨てられ (abandonment). Keeping one's distance raises the fear of abandonment; closer involvement raises the risk of entrapment. The other pairs are not mentioned.

items.stem: How does the writer regard keeping channels of dialogue open?
choices: As a sign of weakness that may encourage the other side to attack.
As less important than building up military strength.
As essential to lasting deterrence, not as weakness.
As useful only after fighting has already broken out.
items.explanation: The last sentence says it is 弱腰ではなく (not weak-kneed) but an indispensable condition for sustainable deterrence. A is explicitly denied; B contradicts the claim that the key lies less in the balance of power; D is wrong because dialogue is meant to stop misunderstandings before they become crises.

items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?
choices: The issue is not whether to allow surveillance but how to limit it with real checks.
All surveillance by intelligence agencies should be banned, because privacy must come first.
Security matters more than privacy, so monitoring of communications should be widely expanded.
Citizens who worry about terrorism are being irrational and should not shape security policy.
items.explanation: The fourth paragraph states that the issue is not a yes-or-no choice but where to draw the line (誰が、何を根拠に、どこまで), with prior judicial review, later independent checks and eventual disclosure. B is rejected as unrealistic; C ignores the essay's defense of privacy; D contradicts the first paragraph, which says citizens' wish for safety cannot be dismissed.

items.stem: Why does the writer reject the idea that people with nothing to hide have nothing to fear?
choices: Because criminals always find ways around monitoring, so surveillance burdens only the innocent.
Because it sees privacy only as a way to hide wrongdoing, ignoring its role in free thought.
Because surveillance technology is too expensive for the small number of plots it stops.
Because most people do have something to hide, even if it is not actually illegal.
items.explanation: The writer says the argument 取り違えている (mistakes) privacy for a right to keep secrets, whereas free thought and expression need a space where one is not observed, and being watched makes people self-censor. A, C and D are not arguments made in the text: the essay does not discuss criminals evading monitoring, cost, or what most people have to hide.

items.stem: What point is the writer making with 「今日の政府が善意であっても、明日の政府がそうである保証はない」?
choices: The current government is secretly misusing the information it has already collected.
Governments change so often that no surveillance policy can be carried out consistently.
Citizens should vote out any government that tries to expand its powers of surveillance.
Systems must be designed so that future operators cannot abuse them.
items.explanation: The next sentence draws the conclusion: systems must be designed so they cannot be abused even when the people running them change. A contradicts the premise that today's government may be well-meaning; B and C go beyond the text.

items.stem: In the fourth paragraph, what does 歯止め refer to?
choices: tools that make surveillance faster
punishments for people who criticize the government
secret agreements between agencies
safeguards that stop surveillance from going too far
items.explanation: 歯止め is literally a brake or stopper and figuratively a check that keeps something from escalating. Here it refers to the listed controls: judicial review, independent verification and later disclosure. The other options do not fit a list of oversight measures.

items.stem: What is the essay's main idea?
choices: Modern technology should be given up so that people can return to a slower and richer life.
Convenience is not the problem; making efficiency the only value is.
People are busier today mainly because they work longer hours than in the past.
Letters are a better form of communication than e-mail because waiting for a reply is valuable.
items.explanation: The fourth and fifth paragraphs say the problem is not convenience itself but treating it as the sole standard of value, and that consciously choosing what to omit and what to keep is the key. A is rejected: idealizing the past and denying convenience is called 的外れ. C is not one of the explanations given (rising expectations and lost processes). D turns one example of 'time spent waiting' into a general claim the writer never makes.

items.stem: What is the first explanation the writer offers for why people feel busier?
choices: Modern devices break down more often than older ones, and fixing them takes time.
People now have fewer holidays than before because work has become more demanding.
Convenience removes the processes in which rich time used to be found.
Time saved through efficiency is filled with new tasks, and expectations rise.
items.explanation: The second paragraph gives the first explanation: saved time is immediately filled with new tasks, and faster communication raises expectations of fast replies. C is the writer's second, 'more fundamental' explanation, not the first. A and B are not mentioned.

items.stem: In the fourth paragraph, the writer says denying convenience would be 的外れ. What does this mean?
choices: exactly right
too emotional
missing the point
too expensive
items.explanation: 的外れ (literally 'off the target') means beside the point or misguided. The writer uses it to reject idealizing the past, then immediately lists the great benefits of convenience. It is the opposite of A, and B and D are unrelated meanings.

items.stem: What is the writer's main point?
choices: The culture of reading the air should be abandoned because it is the cause of most scandals.
Japanese society should return to a time when everyone shared the same values and experiences.
Reading the air has value, but should be balanced with saying things clearly.
People from abroad who work in Japan must learn to read the air as well as Japanese people do.
items.explanation: The writer lists benefits and costs, then says the culture should not be discarded; instead, sensing and verbalizing should be rebalanced (察したうえで、あえて言葉にして確かめる). A is explicitly rejected (筆者はそうは考えない). B is never proposed. D reverses the argument: expecting others to sense everything places an excessive burden on them.

items.stem: How does the writer connect reading the air with organizational scandals?
choices: Scandals happen when people read the air too little and act without thinking of others.
Unspoken doubts pile up in silence, so problems go ahead unchecked.
Scandals are caused by colleagues from other countries who cannot read the air.
Reading the air helps organizations notice and uncover scandals at an early stage.
items.explanation: The third paragraph says that where reading the air is expected, dissent is rare, everyone doubts but nobody speaks, and many scandals arise from such accumulated silence. A and D reverse this link, and C is not claimed; foreign colleagues are mentioned only in the discussion of diversity.

items.stem: According to the writer, when does reading the air work well?
choices: When the group is very large.
When people speak several languages.
When a strong leader gives clear orders.
When members share the same values and experiences.
items.explanation: The fourth paragraph says it functions only when members share values and experiences (同じ価値観や経験を共有している場合に限られる). Different mother tongues are given as a condition that undermines it (B), and group size and leadership are not mentioned.

items.stem: Which best describes the writer's stance toward reading the air?
choices: Wholly critical, seeing no value in the practice.
Balanced, recognizing both its value and its costs.
Nostalgic and uncritical.
Humorous and mocking.
items.explanation: The essay devotes a paragraph to its advantages, two to its costs, and ends by defending the ability to sense others as a form of imagination while asking for balance. A ignores the stated advantages, C ignores the criticism, and nothing in the calm, argumentative style is humorous (D).

items.stem: What is the writer's main argument?
choices: The base should drop the extension entirely, because the residents were living there first.
Night training is clearly necessary, so residents should accept the extra burden.
The real problem is a decision process that consulted residents only after the fact.
The press is chiefly to blame for reporting the plan before the city was told.
items.explanation: The writer rejects the either/or debate and says 「問われているのは、決定に至る過程である」, defining consent as being heard 「結論が出る前に」. The residents' prior presence explains their view but is not used to demand cancellation; necessity is granted but said not to settle the matter; and the press is not blamed.

items.stem: What does the writer imply by saying the night quiet was 「交渉によって与えられたものではなく、もともとそこにあったもの」?
choices: Since residents never negotiated with the base, they have no standing now.
Losing it feels like having something taken, not like being refused a favor.
The base had once promised residents that their nights would stay quiet.
The quiet was a benefit that residents had received in return for hosting the base.
items.explanation: Framing quiet as something that 「もともとそこにあった」 means residents are being asked to give up what was already theirs, which is why 「少しは我慢を」 obscures the uneven burden. The writer does not deny their standing, mentions no promise, and explicitly says it was not something given in exchange.

items.stem: What is the writer's attitude toward the base's explanation of why the training is needed?
choices: It is a mere pretext for expanding the base's activities.
It is hard to refute, but it does not answer the question of consent.
It is fully convincing, so the residents ought to accept a compromise now.
It was made in bad faith, as the leak to the press shows.
items.explanation: The writer calls it 「明快」 and says 「この論理に反論するのは難しい」, then turns with 「しかし、必要性が認められることと…受け入れることとは、別の問題」. The writer also says 「基地側に悪意があったとは思わない」, ruling out bad faith or pretext.

items.stem: What is the function of the final paragraph?
choices: To note that both sides assume the base will stay, so they should settle future procedures.
To argue that residents most affected by noise should be offered help to relocate.
To predict that the base will eventually be moved elsewhere because of growing local opposition.
To conclude that the extension debate is pointless since the base is not leaving.
items.explanation: Because both sides share the 「前提」 that the base remains, the writer urges turning the dispute into 「次の決定の手順を双方で話し合う機会」. Relocation of residents or the base is never suggested, and the debate is treated as an opportunity, not as pointless.

items.stem: What is the main conclusion of the briefing note?
choices: The town mishandled the disaster response and should be kept out of future joint planning exercises.
The dispatch should have lasted even longer for the sake of residents' peace of mind.
Water supply should go to private contractors from the very start of any disaster.
The problems reflect weak peacetime role-sharing, so procedures should be built with the town.
items.explanation: The note says the issues are 「町の対応の不備というより、平時から役割分担を確認する場が十分でなかったことの表れ」 and proposes joint exercises and criteria 「町と共に作る」. It does not blame or exclude the town, it argues the water mission ran too long rather than too short, and contractors are relevant only once available.

items.stem: Why does the note mention the three requirements for disaster dispatch?
choices: To argue that the town's original request for help had been legally invalid from the start.
To explain why the unit took several days to arrive in the town after the landslides had occurred.
To show that continuing water supply once alternatives existed went beyond its proper scope.
To criticize residents for demanding more support than the law allowed them to receive.
items.explanation: The note links 「非代替性」 to the point that 「代わりの手段がある段階で活動を続けること」 could weaken readiness elsewhere. The initial request is not questioned, there is no arrival delay, and the pressure came from the town, not residents, whose wish for 「安心」 is called understandable.

items.stem: What risk does the writer see in sharing withdrawal criteria with the town?
choices: The town might refuse to disclose its own criteria for requesting help.
The criteria might be too complicated for the town's staff to apply during a real crisis.
Criteria presented unilaterally could read as a notice of limits and harm trust.
Sharing the criteria might reveal sensitive details of unit operations.
items.explanation: The note warns that if the criteria are taken as 「『ここまでしかやらない』という通告」 they will 「かえって信頼を損なう」, hence they should not be 「一方的に示す」. Complexity, reciprocity and secrecy are not raised.

items.stem: How does the writer interpret the chairman's words 「あんたが来たなら、仕方ないな」?
choices: As an angry admission that the chairman had no power to refuse the change
As acceptance granted because he came in person, not because of the change itself
As a judgment that the change was reasonable once its causes had been properly explained
As a polite way of ending the conversation without discussing the change
items.explanation: The writer says 「会長が受け入れたのは、変更そのものではなく、変更を伝えに来た人間だった」 and that the words were both forgiveness and 「一種の条件」. Nothing suggests anger, a judgment on the change's merits, or a brush-off.

items.stem: What is the essay's central point?
choices: Advance notice mainly conveys regard, and trust attaches to particular people.
Written notices are sufficient, and phone calls waste the liaison's limited time.
Liaison officers should rotate often so that trust does not depend on one person.
Higher units should never change a schedule on only a single day's notice.
items.explanation: The writer concludes that what is delivered is 「『あなた方のことを忘れていない』という姿勢」 and that 「信頼は案外、特定の顔に結びついている」. The inefficiency charge came from young personnel and was rejected; rotation and rules for higher units are not proposed.

items.stem: What feeling is expressed in the last two sentences?
choices: Pride that his personal approach has become standard practice in the unit
Regret that he relied on phone calls instead of proper written notices
Confidence that whoever now makes the calls is doing the job well
Unease about whether the trust he built has carried over to his successor
items.explanation: 「気にならないと言えば嘘になる」 is an understated admission of worry, following his point that personal trust is also a 「危うさ」 when people change. He says nothing about his method becoming standard, does not regret calling, and expresses no confidence in the successor.

script.speaker: 駅員
script.text: まもなく、二番線に快速、東京行きがまいります。危ないですから、黄色い線の内側までお下がりください。

script.speaker: 店内放送
script.text: 本日もご来店いただき、誠にありがとうございます。当店は、まもなく午後九時で閉店いたします。お会計はお早めにお願いいたします。

script.speaker: 警備員
script.text: こちらは正門です。車でお越しの方は、一度止まって、身分証明書をご用意ください。

script.speaker: 職員
script.text: こちらは避難所です。毛布と水は、入口の受付で受け取ってください。お一人様、毛布一枚、水二本です。

script.speaker: 車内放送
script.text: 次は、市役所前です。お降りの方は、ボタンを押してください。

script.speaker: 田中
script.text: もしもし、田中です。明日の会議は、午前十時から午後二時に変わりました。場所は同じ、三階の会議室です。よろしくお願いします。

script.speaker: 受付
script.text: 山本歯科です。ご予約は、三月五日、金曜日の午前十一時です。変更の場合は、お電話ください。

script.speaker: 市役所
script.text: 市民の皆様にお知らせします。明日、七月十日は、水道工事のため、午前九時から正午まで水が出ません。飲み水は、今日のうちにご用意ください。ご協力をお願いします。

script.speaker: 放送
script.text: 基地内の皆さんにお知らせします。本日は、食堂の工事のため、昼食を第二体育館で配ります。時間はいつもと同じ、十一時半から一時までです。お弁当の箱は、食べたあと、体育館の入口に返してください。

passages.title: Asking the way to the post office

script.speaker: A
script.text: すみません、郵便局はどこですか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 郵便局ですか。この道をまっすぐ行って、二つ目の信号を右に曲がってください。銀行の隣にありますよ。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 二つ目の信号を右ですね。歩いて何分ぐらいですか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 五分ぐらいです。

script.speaker: A
script.text: ありがとうございます。

script.speaker: 店員
script.text: いらっしゃいませ。何かお探しですか。

script.speaker: 客
script.text: このジャケットの、もう少し大きいサイズはありますか。

script.speaker: 店員
script.text: はい、Lサイズがございます。色は黒と紺がありますが。

script.speaker: 客
script.text: じゃあ、紺をお願いします。試着してもいいですか。

script.speaker: 店員
script.text: はい、試着室はあちらです。

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: 木村さん、来週の打ち合わせ、いつがいいですか。

script.speaker: 木村
script.text: 月曜日は出張なので、火曜日か水曜日がいいです。

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: 火曜日は、私が午後から会議なんです。水曜日の午前十時はどうですか。

script.speaker: 木村
script.text: 大丈夫です。じゃあ、水曜日の十時に、第一会議室で。

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: はい。部屋を予約しておきます。

script.speaker: ゆき
script.text: もしもし、ゆきです。ごめんね、土曜日のランチ、急に仕事が入って、行けなくなっちゃった。日曜日のお昼はどう？駅前のイタリアンのお店、日曜日もやってるみたい。あとでメッセージちょうだい。

script.speaker: 領事部
script.text: こちらは、日本大使館の領事部です。お申し込みのパスポートの準備ができました。平日の午前九時から午後四時までに、受け取りに来てください。そのときに、申請の控えと身分証明書をお持ちください。

script.speaker: 当直
script.text: 全隊員に連絡します。明日予定していた防災訓練は、雨の予報のため、あさっての木曜日に延期します。集合の時間と場所は変わりません。午前八時に、本部前の広場に集まってください。なお、木曜日に当直の人は、訓練に参加しなくてもかまいません。当直の交代について質問がある人は、総務の中村さんまで連絡してください。

script.speaker: 市役所
script.text: 市役所からのお知らせです。台風十五号が近づいているため、明日、九月十二日は、市内のすべての図書館と市民プールを休館とします。市役所の窓口は開いていますが、午後三時で閉めます。また、市内の小学校と中学校は休校になります。最新の情報は、市のホームページでご確認ください。不要な外出は、できるだけ控えてください。

passages.title: Visitor check-in at a government building

script.speaker: 案内
script.text: ご来庁の皆様にご案内いたします。庁舎に入る際は、一階の受付で身分証明書を提示し、入館証をお受け取りください。入館証は、庁舎内では常に首から下げてください。大きな荷物は、受付の横のロッカーに預けていただきます。お帰りの際は、入館証を必ず受付にお返しください。なお、庁舎内の一部の場所では写真撮影が禁止されていますので、ご注意ください。ご協力をお願いいたします。

script.speaker: 鈴木
script.text: 林さん、引っ越したんですって？新しい部屋はどうですか。

script.speaker: 林
script.text: 前より駅から遠くなったんですけど、広くて静かなので気に入っています。

script.speaker: 鈴木
script.text: 通勤は大変になりませんでしたか。

script.speaker: 林
script.text: 電車は同じ線なので、そんなに変わりません。ただ、駅まで自転車で十分ぐらいかかるんです。前は歩いて五分だったんですけどね。

script.speaker: 鈴木
script.text: それだと、雨の日は大変ですね。

script.speaker: 林
script.text: そうなんです。雨の日は、バスに乗ろうと思っています。

script.speaker: 受付
script.text: こんにちは。今日はどうされましたか。

script.speaker: 患者
script.text: 三日前から、せきが止まらなくて。熱も少しあります。

script.speaker: 受付
script.text: 保険証はお持ちですか。

script.speaker: 患者
script.text: はい、これです。こちらは初めてなんですが。

script.speaker: 受付
script.text: では、こちらの問診票にご記入ください。今、四人お待ちなので、三十分ほどお待ちいただくと思います。

script.speaker: 患者
script.text: わかりました。薬局は、この近くにありますか。

script.speaker: 受付
script.text: はい、隣のビルの一階にあります。

passages.title: Train or car for a weekend trip

script.speaker: A
script.text: 週末の温泉旅行、車で行く？電車で行く？

script.speaker: B
script.text: 車のほうが荷物は楽だけど、土曜日の朝は道が混むからなあ。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 電車なら二時間で着くし、特急の中でお弁当も食べられるよ。

script.speaker: B
script.text: そうだね。でも、駅から旅館まではどうするの？

script.speaker: A
script.text: 旅館のバスが、駅まで迎えに来てくれるって。

script.speaker: B
script.text: じゃあ、電車にしよう。切符は僕が予約しておくね。

script.speaker: A
script.text: ありがとう。帰りの切符もお願いね。

script.speaker: B
script.text: わかった。日曜日の夕方の特急でいいかな。

script.speaker: 大川
script.text: もしもし、ひかり不動産の大川です。先日ご連絡いただいた、お風呂のお湯が出ない件ですが、修理の業者が、明日の午後一時から三時の間に伺います。作業は一時間ほどかかるそうです。作業の間は、お湯だけでなく水も使えなくなりますので、ご了承ください。当日は、業者が伺う前に、私からもう一度お電話します。ご都合が悪い場合は、今日の六時までにお電話ください。よろしくお願いいたします。

passages.title: Medical team for an earthquake-hit country

script.speaker: 報道官
script.text: 本日の会見を始めます。先週、大規模な地震が発生したミナト共和国に対し、政府は国際緊急援助隊として、自衛隊の医療チームおよそ八十人を派遣することを決定しました。チームは明後日の朝に出発し、現地の病院と協力して、けが人の治療や感染症の予防にあたります。活動期間は、現時点では一か月程度を予定しています。また、航空自衛隊の輸送機で、テントや浄水装置などの物資も運びます。

script.speaker: 記者
script.text: 現地の治安については、どのように把握していますか。

script.speaker: 報道官
script.text: 現地の治安は比較的安定していると聞いています。ただし、余震が続いていますので、隊員の安全を最優先に、現地政府や国連機関と緊密に連絡を取りながら活動する方針です。

passages.title: Heavy rain: villages cut off, SDF requested

script.speaker: アナウンサー
script.text: ニュースをお伝えします。記録的な大雨が続いている北浜県では、昨夜から土砂崩れが相次ぎ、山あいの三つの集落が孤立した状態になっています。県によりますと、およそ百二十人が集落に取り残されていますが、これまでにけが人の情報は入っていないということです。北浜県の知事は今朝、陸上自衛隊に災害派遣を要請しました。自衛隊は、ヘリコプターを使って食料や水を運ぶとともに、道路の復旧作業にあたる予定です。気象台によりますと、雨は今夜にかけて降り続く見込みで、県は、川や崖の近くに住む人に対し、明るいうちに避難するよう呼びかけています。なお、北浜県を通る高速道路は、一部の区間で通行止めが続いています。

passages.title: Cyberattack on a city water utility

script.speaker: アナウンサー
script.text: 次のニュースです。南川市の水道局は、浄水場を管理するコンピューターシステムが、外部からサイバー攻撃を受けたと発表しました。水道局によりますと、おととい夜、システムに不正なアクセスがあり、一部の画面が操作できなくなりました。職員がすぐに手動での運転に切り替えたため、水の供給や水質に影響は出ていないということです。攻撃に使われた経路はまだわかっておらず、警察が、不正アクセス禁止法違反の疑いで調べています。また、国の専門機関も職員を派遣し、原因の分析を進めています。水道局は、しばらくの間、システムをインターネットから切り離して運用するとしています。市民からは不安の声も上がっており、専門家は、重要なインフラを守る対策を急ぐ必要があると指摘しています。

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: 木村さん、来週火曜日の関係省庁との打ち合わせなんですが、先方から、水曜日の午後に変更できないかという連絡がありました。

script.speaker: 木村
script.text: 水曜の午後か。午後二時からなら大丈夫だけど、会議室は空いてるかな。

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: 確認したら、第三会議室が二時から四時まで空いていました。仮で押さえておきましたよ。

script.speaker: 木村
script.text: ありがとう。それと、今回は外部の人が六人来るから、入館証の申請が必要だね。

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: はい。申請は前日の正午までなので、名前と所属を今日中に送ってもらうよう、先方にお願いしておきます。

script.speaker: 木村
script.text: 助かる。あと、資料は事前に送るの？

script.speaker: 佐藤
script.text: いえ、機密に関わる部分があるので、当日、会議室で配って、終わったら回収することになっています。

script.speaker: 木村
script.text: わかった。じゃあ、部数は多めに用意しておいて。

script.speaker: 山口
script.text: 中島さん、今度の日曜日の防災訓練、参加されますか。

script.speaker: 中島
script.text: ええ、そのつもりです。今年は何をするんでしたっけ。

script.speaker: 山口
script.text: 朝九時に公民館に集まって、まず消火器の使い方を練習します。そのあと、小学校の体育館まで歩いて、避難所の開き方を確認するそうです。

script.speaker: 中島
script.text: 去年は雨で中止になりましたよね。

script.speaker: 山口
script.text: そうなんです。だから今年は、雨が降っても体育館の中だけで行うと聞きました。

script.speaker: 中島
script.text: それはいいですね。うちの母も連れて行きたいんですが、足が悪くて、長い距離は歩けないんです。

script.speaker: 山口
script.text: それなら、町内会の車で体育館まで送ってくれるそうですよ。前の日までに会長さんに連絡すればいいはずです。

script.speaker: 中島
script.text: そうですか、助かります。今夜、電話してみます。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 今日は、山岳救助にドローンを導入した西山市消防本部の田中隊長にお話を伺います。導入してどのくらいになりますか。

script.speaker: 田中
script.text: 去年の春からですので、一年半ほどになります。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 効果はいかがですか。

script.speaker: 田中
script.text: 一番大きいのは、捜索の時間が短くなったことです。以前は隊員が何時間も歩いて探していましたが、今は熱を感知するカメラを積んだドローンで、広い範囲を一度に調べられます。去年の冬には、道に迷った登山者を、通報からわずか四十分で見つけることができました。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 難しい点はありますか。

script.speaker: 田中
script.text: 風が強い日や雪が激しい日には飛ばせないことです。ですから、ドローンはあくまで道具の一つで、最後は人の力が必要です。今は、操縦できる隊員を増やすための訓練に力を入れています。

passages.title: A strawberry farm hires workers from abroad

script.speaker: 記者
script.text: 石井さんのイチゴ農園では、今年から海外からの働き手を受け入れているそうですね。

script.speaker: 石井
script.text: はい。ベトナムから来た三人の若者が、春から一緒に働いています。この地域では若い人が都会に出てしまって、収穫の時期に人手が足りなくなっていたんです。

script.speaker: 記者
script.text: 言葉の問題はありませんでしたか。

script.speaker: 石井
script.text: 最初は大変でした。でも、作業の手順を写真付きの説明書にしたら、ずいぶん分かりやすくなったと言われました。今は私のほうが、ベトナム語を少しずつ習っています。

script.speaker: 記者
script.text: これからの計画を教えてください。

script.speaker: 石井
script.text: 来年は、近所の農家と一緒に、働き手が住める寮を建てたいと思っています。一つの農家だけでは、費用が大きすぎますから。

passages.title: Phone call: late-night noise from the training area

script.speaker: A
script.text: もしもし、潮見町役場住民生活課の佐藤と申します。北浜駐屯地の広報室でしょうか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: はい、広報室の中村です。いつもお世話になっております。

script.speaker: A
script.text: お世話になっております。実は今朝、南地区の住民の方から、昨日の夜遅くまで演習場のほうから大きな音がしていたというお電話がありまして。何時ごろまで訓練をされていたか、確認させていただけますか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 申し訳ございません。昨日は夜間の移動訓練がありまして、予定では午後9時に終わるはずでした。ただ、途中で車両が1台故障しまして、最後の部隊が演習場を出たのは午後10時半ごろでした。

script.speaker: A
script.text: そうでしたか。住民の方は、音そのものよりも、いつ終わるのか分からなかったのが不安だったとおっしゃっていました。

script.speaker: B
script.text: ご迷惑をおかけしました。予定より遅れる場合には、町にもご連絡すべきでした。今後は、終了が30分以上遅れる見込みになった時点で、役場の当直にお電話するようにいたします。

script.speaker: A
script.text: ありがとうございます。それから、今週の金曜日にも同じような訓練があると聞いているのですが。

script.speaker: B
script.text: はい、金曜日は午後8時に終了の予定です。念のため、明日、南地区の自治会長さんにも私から直接ご説明に伺います。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 助かります。では、住民の方にはそのようにお伝えします。

passages.title: Radio news: SDF water supply in Okutani

script.speaker: A
script.text: 次のニュースです。大雨の被害を受けた奥谷町では、昨日から自衛隊による給水支援が始まりました。現地から山下記者の報告です。

script.speaker: B
script.text: はい、奥谷町の中央公民館の前に来ています。こちらでは今朝7時から、陸上自衛隊の給水車3台が並び、住民の方々がポリタンクや水のボトルを手に列を作っています。町では、浄水場が土砂で壊れたため、およそ1,200世帯で水道が止まっています。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 給水はいつまで続く見込みですか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 町によりますと、浄水場の復旧には少なくとも1週間かかる見通しで、その間、給水は毎日午前7時から午後6時まで行われます。また、自分で水を取りに来ることが難しいお年寄りの世帯には、隊員と町の職員が一緒に水を届けているということです。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 住民の方の様子はいかがですか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 水を受け取りに来た70代の女性は「水が出ないのがいちばんつらかった。本当に助かります」と話していました。一方で、町の山側の地区では道路がまだ通れないため、給水車が入れない場所も残っています。自衛隊は、明日からヘリコプターで水を運ぶことも検討しているということです。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 山下さん、ありがとうございました。

passages.title: First joint naval exercise draws a neighbor's protest

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: 海上自衛隊と東洋連邦の海軍による初めての共同訓練が、きょうから五日間の日程で始まりました。訓練には艦艇あわせて六隻が参加し、遭難した船の捜索や救助、通信の手順などを確認します。この訓練について、隣国の北陵国の外務省は「地域の緊張を高める」として懸念を表明しました。解説委員の森さんです。

script.speaker: 森
script.text: 今回の訓練の内容を見ると、捜索救助や通信といった、いわば基本的な分野が中心です。政府としては、特定の国を想定したものではないと説明することで、周辺国への配慮を示したと言えます。

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: それでも、北陵国は反発しています。

script.speaker: 森
script.text: 北陵国には、この地域で日本と東洋連邦の協力が深まること自体を警戒する見方があります。ですから、訓練の中身にかかわらず、反発は予想されていたと思います。大事なのは、訓練の目的を丁寧に説明し続けること、そして、北陵国とも防衛当局どうしの対話の窓口を保つことでしょう。偶発的な衝突を防ぐうえで、こうした連絡の仕組みは欠かせません。地域の安定のためには、相互理解と信頼を地道に積み重ねるしかないでしょう。

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: 西海国との漁業交渉は、きのうまでの三日間の協議でも合意に至りませんでした。現地で取材している小林記者です。

script.speaker: 小林
script.text: はい。今回の交渉の焦点は、両国の水域が重なる海域で、どちらの漁船がどれだけ魚を取れるかという点でした。日本側は去年と同じ漁獲量を求めましたが、西海国側は、資源が減っていることを理由に、全体の量を三割減らすよう主張しました。

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: 話し合いは物別れに終わった、ということですか。

script.speaker: 小林
script.text: いえ、完全な決裂ではありません。両国は来月、専門家による資源調査を共同で行うことでは一致しました。ただし、漁獲量をめぐる双方の主張の隔たりは、依然として大きいままです。関係者の間では、調査の結果をもとに、双方が歩み寄るための時間を確保した、という見方が出ています。ただ、漁業者にとっては、漁の季節が始まる前に結論が出ないことへの不安が大きく、政府は難しいかじ取りを迫られそうです。

passages.title: A higher seawall or moving uphill?

script.speaker: 青木
script.text: 東浦地区の防潮堤をさらに三メートル高くする計画には、私は賛成できません。工事費は二百億円を超える見込みですし、完成まで十年かかります。その間に大きな津波が来たらどうするのか。むしろ、住宅の高台への移転を支援するほうが、住民の命を確実に守れると考えます。現実的な選択肢として、真剣に議論すべきです。

script.speaker: 藤原
script.text: 青木さんの懸念はわかります。ただ、東浦には漁港があって、漁業者は海の近くに住み、働き続けたいと考えています。移転を進めれば、地域の産業、ひいては暮らしの基盤そのものが成り立たなくなる恐れがあるんです。

script.speaker: 青木
script.text: 全員を移転させるべきだと言っているわけではありません。高台に住まいを移しても、港には通えます。仕事の場所と住む場所を分けるという考え方です。

script.speaker: 藤原
script.text: それは一つの方法だと思います。しかし、高齢の漁業者にとって、毎日坂を上り下りするのは簡単ではありません。私は、防潮堤の工事を進めながら、避難路の整備も急ぐという、両方の対策が必要だと思います。

script.speaker: 青木
script.text: 両方となると、費用はさらに膨らみます。限られた予算の中で、優先順位をはっきりさせるべきです。

passages.title: Do schools still need foreign languages?

script.speaker: 西田
script.text: 翻訳アプリの精度は、この数年で大きく上がりました。旅行や簡単な仕事のやり取りなら、もう困ることはほとんどありません。これからの学校は、外国語の文法を細かく教えるより、その時間をほかの教科に回してもいいのではないでしょうか。

script.speaker: 松本
script.text: 翻訳の技術が便利なのは確かです。でも、言葉を学ぶ価値は、情報を伝えることだけではないと思うんです。相手の言葉で話そうとすることで信頼関係が生まれることもありますし、別の言語の構造を知ることで、自分の母語を見直すきっかけにもなります。

script.speaker: 西田
script.text: おっしゃることはわかりますが、授業時間は限られていますから、優先順位をつけなければなりません。全員に同じレベルを求める必要はないと思います。

script.speaker: 松本
script.text: その点は私も同じ意見です。全員が通訳を目指す必要はありません。ただ、機械に任せきりにすると、訳が正しいかどうかを評価する力も育たなくなります。道具を使いこなすためにも、基礎は必要だと考えます。

passages.title: Has remote work helped regional towns?

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: コロナ禍をきっかけに広がったリモートワークですが、ここ数年、地方に移住する人の数は伸び悩んでいます。大野さん、この傾向をどう見ていますか。

script.speaker: 大野
script.text: 一時的なブームが落ち着いた、というのが正直なところだと思います。多くの企業が週に何日かは出社を求めるようになりましたから、完全に地方に移るのは難しいんですね。

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: では、地方にとってリモートワークの効果は限られていた、ということでしょうか。

script.speaker: 大野
script.text: いえ、私はそうは考えていません。確かに、移住者の数だけを見れば期待外れかもしれません。しかし、都市に住みながら週末は地方で過ごす「二地域居住」は着実に増えています。そうした人たちが地元の店を利用し、祭りの担い手になっている例も少なくありません。

script.speaker: キャスター
script.text: 数字には表れにくい変化だと。

script.speaker: 大野
script.text: そうです。人口という一つの指標だけで評価すると、大事な変化を見落とす恐れがあります。自治体も、移住者を増やすことだけを課題とするのではなく、地域とかかわる人をどう増やすかという視点を持つべきでしょう。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 最近、病院がサイバー攻撃を受けて、診療を止めざるを得なくなるケースが相次いでいます。なぜ病院が狙われるのでしょうか。

script.speaker: 高橋
script.text: 一つは、止まると困るシステムを抱えているからです。電子カルテが使えなくなれば、診療そのものができません。攻撃する側は、早く復旧したい病院ならお金を払うだろうと考えるわけです。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 対策が遅れている理由は何でしょう。

script.speaker: 高橋
script.text: 多くの病院では、システムの担当者が一人か二人しかいません。しかも、メーカーの異なる古い医療機器がたくさんつながっていて、全体を把握すること自体が難しいんです。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: では、何から始めればいいでしょうか。

script.speaker: 高橋
script.text: まず、データのバックアップを、ネットワークから切り離して保管しておくことです。これだけで、被害を受けても数日で診療を再開できる可能性が高まります。完璧な防御はありません。攻撃を受ける前提で、いかに早く立ち直るかを考えることが大切です。

passages.title: Coordination meeting: convoy and the school run

script.speaker: A
script.text: 本日はお時間をいただき、ありがとうございます。さっそくですが、来月の車両移動の件です。資料では、午前7時半から8時半の間に、大型車両12台が市道中央線を通る計画になっていますね。

script.speaker: B
script.text: はい。演習の開始時刻から逆算すると、その時間帯に出発する必要がありまして。

script.speaker: A
script.text: ご事情は理解します。ただ、その時間帯は中央小学校の登校時間とちょうど重なります。あの道は歩道が狭く、保護者からも以前から懸念の声が出ています。子どもの安全を何より重視する立場から、市としては、このままの計画ではお受けしにくいというのが正直なところです。

script.speaker: B
script.text: なるほど。時間をずらすとなると演習全体の日程に影響が出るので、私の判断ではすぐにはお答えできません。ただ、経路の変更であれば、検討の余地があると思います。例えば、県道を使って学校の前を避けられないか、基地に持ち帰って確認します。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 県道を使っていただけるなら、双方にとって現実的な妥協案になりそうです。距離は少し長くなりますか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 10分ほど余計にかかる計算ですが、出発を少し早めれば吸収できるかもしれません。それでも中央線を通らざるを得ない場合には、交差点ごとに誘導員を置き、車両の間隔を空けて通行させる案も併せてお示しします。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 分かりました。どちらの案になるにしても、保護者への説明は早めにしたいので、来週の金曜日までにお返事をいただけますか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 承知しました。市のご懸念はよく分かりましたので、金曜日までに必ずご連絡します。

passages.title: Radio interview: a base commander on community relations

script.speaker: A
script.text: 今日は、北浜駐屯地の石川司令にお話を伺います。司令に着任されて1年ですが、地域との関係で特に力を入れてきたことは何でしょうか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 着任した当初、私が一番気になったのは、駐屯地のことをよく知らないという住民の方が意外に多かったことです。騒音の苦情はあっても、中で何をしているのかが分からない。分からないから不安になる、ということだと思いました。そこで、月に一度の見学会を始め、隊員が地元の学校や祭りにも積極的に出ていくようにしました。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 反応はいかがでしたか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 見学会には、この1年で延べ2千人ほどが来てくださいました。ただ、正直に申し上げると、見学に来てくださるのは、もともと自衛隊に関心のある方が多い。本当に声を聞くべきなのは、来てくださらない方々なんです。

script.speaker: A
script.text: そういった方々とは、どのように接点を持っているのですか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 自治会の会合に、こちらから出向いてお話を伺うようにしています。そこでは厳しいご意見もいただきます。ヘリの音で赤ちゃんが起きてしまう、という話を聞いたときには、数字の上での苦情の件数とは違う重みを感じました。

script.speaker: A
script.text: そうしたご意見は、実際の訓練に反映されているのでしょうか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: すべてにお応えできるわけではありません。訓練の必要性は変わりませんから。ただ、飛行経路の見直しなど、できることはやってきたつもりです。できないことについても、なぜできないのかを説明する責任があると考えています。それが信頼の土台になると思っています。

passages.title: Refugee acceptance: numbers and support together

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: 今日は、難民の受け入れについて考えてみたいと思います。わが国が昨年、難民として認定した人の数は、申請者全体のごく一部にとどまりました。政府は、審査は法律にのっとって厳格かつ公正に行っていると説明しています。確かに、制度を悪用する申請を見抜くことは必要です。しかし、厳格さを強調するあまり、本当に保護を必要とする人まで門前払いにしてはいないか、という疑問はぬぐえません。人権の観点からも、審査の透明性を高めることが求められます。

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: よく聞かれるのは、受け入れを増やせば治安が悪化する、あるいは社会の一体感が損なわれる、という懸念です。こうした不安を頭から否定するのは、建設的ではないでしょう。ただ、受け入れた人を地域で孤立させれば、その懸念がかえって現実のものになりかねません。言葉を学ぶ場や仕事に就く機会を用意し、地域の一員として迎え入れる体制があってはじめて、共存は可能になるのです。

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: 仮に、受け入れの数だけを増やし、その後の支援を自治体やボランティア任せにするなら、それは形だけの人道主義と言わざるを得ません。逆に、支援の体制が整うまで受け入れを先送りし続けるのも、国際社会の一員としての責務から目をそらすことになります。求められているのは、理念と現実のどちらかを選ぶことではなく、数と支援を車の両輪として同時に進める覚悟ではないでしょうか。

passages.title: The compact city and those left behind

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: 人口が減り続ける地方都市で、住宅や病院、商業施設を中心部に集める「コンパクトシティ」の考え方が広がっています。道路や水道といったインフラを維持する費用を抑え、行政サービスの効率性を高めるという意味で、持続可能なまちづくりに向けた理にかなった政策であることは間違いありません。

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: しかし、この政策には見過ごされがちな側面があります。中心部に移り住む余裕のある人は移っていきますが、郊外に取り残されるのは、多くの場合、車の運転が難しくなった高齢者です。バスの本数が減り、近くの店が閉まれば、暮らしはますます不便になります。効率を追い求めた結果、最も支援が必要な人の生活が脅かされるとしたら、それは政策の目的そのものと矛盾するのではないでしょうか。

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: 一方で、すべての集落を今のまま維持せよというのも、財政の現実を考えれば無責任な主張です。自治体にとっては、まさに痛し痒しの課題です。

script.speaker: 解説委員
script.text: 大切なのは、移転を強いるのではなく、郊外に住み続ける人のための移動手段を確保するなど、選択の余地を残すことでしょう。そして何より、どの地域をどう変えていくのか、その優先順位を、住民との対話を重ねて決めていく過程が欠かせません。行政が描いた図面を上から押しつけるだけでは、どれほど合理的な計画であっても、地域の信頼を失うことになります。

passages.title: How to pay for higher defense spending

script.speaker: 中村
script.text: 政府は、今後五年間で防衛費を大幅に増やす方針を打ち出しましたが、その財源をどうするかという議論は、いまだに決着がついていません。岡田さん、まずこの点をどうご覧になっていますか。

script.speaker: 岡田
script.text: 率直に言って、順番が逆だと思います。本来であれば、どのような脅威に対して何が足りないのかをまず示し、そのうえで必要な額と財源を国民に問うべきです。ところが今回は、金額が先に決まり、中身と財源があとから議論されている。これでは本末転倒と言われても仕方がありません。

script.speaker: 中村
script.text: ただ、周辺の安全保障環境が急速に厳しくなっているという認識は、与野党を問わず、ある程度共有されていますよね。

script.speaker: 岡田
script.text: そこに異論はありません。抑止力を高める必要性自体は、私も認めます。問題は、増税か国債かという財源の選択が、将来の世代に負担を回すかどうかという問題と表裏一体だということです。国債に頼れば、今の有権者は痛みを感じませんが、そのつけは子どもたちに回ります。

script.speaker: 中村
script.text: 一方で、増税となれば、物価高に苦しむ家計にさらに負担をかけることになります。政府としては痛し痒しでしょうね。

script.speaker: 岡田
script.text: まさにそうです。だからこそ、説明責任が問われるんです。どちらを選ぶにしても、なぜその額が必要なのかを丁寧に説明しない限り、国民の理解は得られないでしょう。防衛政策というのは、国民の信頼という土台があってはじめて成り立つものですから。

passages.title: Active cyber defense and the secrecy of communications

script.speaker: 石田
script.text: 重要インフラへのサイバー攻撃は、もはや仮定の話ではありません。攻撃を受けてから対応するのでは遅すぎる。政府が通信の情報を分析し、攻撃の兆候をつかんだ段階で相手のサーバーに入り、無力化する。いわゆる能動的サイバー防御は、国の安全保障にとって避けて通れないと考えます。

script.speaker: 森川
script.text: 脅威が現実のものだという点に異論はありません。ただ、私が危惧しているのは、通信の情報を分析するという部分です。どこまでが「攻撃の兆候」で、どこからが普通の市民の通信なのか。その線引きを政府の裁量に委ねてしまえば、憲法が保障する通信の秘密が形骸化しかねません。

script.speaker: 石田
script.text: 分析の対象は、あくまで通信の中身ではなく、発信元や量といった機械的な情報に限られます。個人のメールを読むわけではありません。

script.speaker: 森川
script.text: そう説明されても、腑に落ちないんです。どんな情報を、誰が、どのくらいの期間保存するのか。それをチェックする独立した機関の権限は、どこまで及ぶのか。そこが法律で明確にされない限り、「限られる」という言葉は、いくらでも広げて解釈できてしまいます。プライバシーを守るには、手続きの透明性が欠かせません。

script.speaker: 石田
script.text: 監視の仕組みが必要だという点は、私も同意します。ただ、手続きを重くしすぎて、一刻を争う場面で動けないのでは、本末転倒です。

script.speaker: 森川
script.text: だからこそ、平時のうちにルールを決めておくべきなんです。有事になってから議論しても、冷静な判断はできませんから。

script.speaker: 野村
script.text: 先月の市長選挙では、候補者の一人が不正な献金を受けていたという偽の動画が、投票の直前に大量に拡散されました。訂正の報道が出たのは、投票が終わったあとです。選挙結果にどれほど影響したかはわかりませんが、有権者の判断がゆがめられた可能性は否定できません。これは民主主義の根幹にかかわる問題です。

script.speaker: 川上
script.text: 技術的に言えば、今の生成AIを使えば、本物と見分けのつかない動画を、誰でも短時間で作れます。見破る技術も進歩していますが、作る側と見破る側のいたちごっこで、決定的な解決策はないのが現状です。

script.speaker: 野村
script.text: だとすれば、プラットフォームの事業者に、投稿の削除をもっと強く義務づけるべきではないでしょうか。報道の信頼性そのものが揺らいでいるという懸念もあります。

script.speaker: 川上
script.text: そこは慎重になるべきだと思います。基準が不透明なまま、何が偽情報かを事業者や政府が判断する仕組みは、使い方を誤れば、都合の悪い言論を封じる道具にもなりかねません。表現の自由との均衡をどう取るのかという問題は、簡単には片づきません。

script.speaker: 野村
script.text: 確かに、削除だけに頼るのは副作用も大きく、危ういですね。そうなると、結局は受け手の側の力を育てるしかないのでしょうか。

script.speaker: 川上
script.text: それが遠回りに見えて、実は一番の近道だと私は考えています。情報の出どころを確かめる習慣を、学校教育の段階から身につけてもらう。もちろん時間はかかりますが、民主主義の土台を守るには、ほかに王道はないと思います。

passages.title: A former diplomat on alliances and transparency

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 杉山さんは長年、同盟国との交渉に携わってこられました。最近、同盟の結束が揺らいでいるという指摘がありますが、どうご覧になりますか。

script.speaker: 杉山
script.text: 同盟が一枚岩だったことなど、実は一度もないんですよ。外から見れば足並みがそろっているようでも、内側では常に利害がぶつかっている。貿易、駐留経費、どこまで役割を分担するのか。それを表に出さずに調整するのが、外交官の仕事でした。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: では、今の状況も特別ではない、と。

script.speaker: 杉山
script.text: 違いがあるとすれば、その不一致が公の場で語られるようになったことでしょう。首脳が、交渉の手の内を記者会見で明かしてしまう。これでは、落としどころを探る余地がなくなります。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 透明性が高まった、という見方もできませんか。

script.speaker: 杉山
script.text: もちろん、国民に説明することは大事です。ただ、交渉の途中経過をすべて公開すれば、双方とも国内向けに強い姿勢を見せざるを得なくなる。結果として、歩み寄りがかえって難しくなるんです。透明性と交渉の柔軟性は、ある意味で二律背反の関係にあると言えるかもしれません。

script.speaker: 聞き手
script.text: 最後に、若い外交官へのメッセージをお願いします。

script.speaker: 杉山
script.text: 相手の立場に立って考えること、でしょうか。相手が自分の国で何を言われるかまで想像できなければ、合意は結べません。月並みですが、結局はこれに尽きると思います。

passages.title: Press briefing: extending night flight training

script.speaker: A
script.text: それでは、定例の記者会見を始めます。まず私から、お知らせが一点あります。来年度から、当基地における夜間飛行訓練の終了時刻を、現在の午後9時から午後10時に変更する方向で、緑川市との調整を始めました。背景には、災害時の夜間救難に対応できる隊員の数を増やす必要があるという事情があります。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 地元紙の小野です。この方針は、市への正式な説明より先に一部で報道されました。市側は「順番が逆だ」と反発していますが、どう受け止めていますか。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 結果として、市や住民の皆様に報道で先に知っていただく形になったことは、大変申し訳なく思っております。情報の管理に不十分な点があったと認識しており、現在、経緯を確認しているところです。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 確認ですが、延長は決定事項なのでしょうか。それとも、市の同意が得られなければ見直す余地があるのでしょうか。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 先ほど申し上げたとおり、変更する方向で調整を始めた段階です。訓練の必要性そのものは変わりませんが、実施の方法、例えば延長する曜日や期間については、市のご意見を伺いながら決めていきたいと考えております。

script.speaker: B
script.text: つまり、延長すること自体は譲れないが、やり方については相談に応じる、という理解でよろしいですか。

script.speaker: A
script.text: そのようにお受け取りいただいても差し支えないかと思います。ただ、地元のご理解なしに訓練を続けることが、現実的には難しいということも、私どもは十分承知しております。

script.speaker: B
script.text: では、理解が得られなかった場合はどうされるのですか。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 仮定のご質問にはお答えを控えさせていただきます。私どもとしては、まず説明を尽くすことに全力を挙げたいと考えております。

passages.title: Discussion: training needs and community consent

script.speaker: A
script.text: 今日は、基地と地域の関係について、県立大学の川端教授と考えます。先生、訓練の必要性と住民の生活、この二つはどうしても対立するものなのでしょうか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 対立する面があるのは確かです。ただ、それを「どちらを取るか」という問題として扱うと、議論は行き詰まると私は考えています。訓練は国全体のためのものですが、騒音は特定の地域が負担している。問題の本質は、その負担の偏りをどう扱うかにあるんです。

script.speaker: A
script.text: その偏りに対しては、国から周辺の自治体に交付金が出ていますよね。それで釣り合いが取れているという見方もあります。

script.speaker: B
script.text: 交付金には一定の意味があります。防音工事や公共施設の整備に使われ、住民の生活を実際に支えている。ただ、お金で負担を埋め合わせるという発想には限界があります。住民が求めているのは、しばしば補償よりも、自分たちの声が決定に届いているという実感なんです。

script.speaker: A
script.text: しかし、住民の声をすべて聞いていたら、訓練は成り立たないのではありませんか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: おっしゃるとおりで、すべての要望に応えることはできません。ですから私は、同意と拒否権を区別すべきだと思っています。住民に拒否権を与えるわけではない。けれども、決定の前に意見を述べる機会があり、その意見がどう扱われたかが説明される。それだけで、結論が同じでも受け止め方はかなり変わります。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 手続きが大事だということですね。ただ、それは結局、決まったことを受け入れさせるための儀式になりませんか。

script.speaker: B
script.text: その危険はあります。形だけの説明会を重ねれば、かえって不信を深めるでしょう。ですから、少なくとも一部の事柄、例えば訓練の時間帯や経路については、住民の意見で実際に変わりうるという余地を残しておく必要がある。何も変わらない話し合いに、人は二度目は来ませんから。

script.speaker: A
script.text: 最後の一言は、重いですね。

items.stem: Where is the arriving train going?
choices: Yokohama
Tokyo
Shinjuku
Ueno
items.explanation: The announcement says 「東京行き」, a train bound for Tokyo. No other destination is mentioned, so Yokohama, Shinjuku and Ueno are wrong.

items.stem: What are passengers asked to do?
choices: Move to platform 1
Buy a rapid-service ticket
Board quickly through all doors
Stay behind the yellow line
items.explanation: 「黄色い線の内側までお下がりください」 asks passengers to step back behind the yellow line. The train arrives at platform 2 (not 1), and nothing is said about tickets or boarding quickly.

items.stem: What time does the store close?
items.explanation: 「午後九時で閉店いたします」 means the store closes at 9:00 p.m. 午後 is p.m., so 9:00 a.m. is wrong, and 8:00 or 10:00 are never mentioned.

items.stem: Why is this announcement made?
choices: To announce a special sale
To tell shoppers the store will close soon
To look for a lost child
To announce a new store opening
items.explanation: 「まもなく…閉店いたします」 and 「お会計はお早めに」 tell shoppers the store is about to close and ask them to pay soon. There is no mention of a sale, a lost child, or a new store.

items.stem: What must people arriving by car do at the main gate?
choices: Stop and have their ID ready
Park outside the gate
Call the duty office
Show a parking ticket
items.explanation: 「一度止まって、身分証明書をご用意ください」 means stop once and prepare your identification. Parking outside, calling an office, and a parking ticket are not mentioned.

items.stem: How many bottles of water does each person receive?
choices: One
Three
Two
Four
items.explanation: 「お一人様、毛布一枚、水二本」: one blanket and two bottles of water per person. "One" is the number of blankets, not bottles.

items.stem: Where are the blankets and water handed out?
choices: In the gymnasium
At City Hall
In the parking lot
At the reception desk by the entrance
items.explanation: 「入口の受付で受け取ってください」 says to collect them at the reception desk at the entrance. The other places are not mentioned.

items.stem: What is the next stop?
choices: The hospital
The train station
City Hall
The post office
items.explanation: 「次は、市役所前です」: the next stop is in front of City Hall (市役所). No hospital, station, or post office is mentioned.

items.stem: What should passengers who want to get off do?
choices: Press the button
Tell the driver
Pay at the front door
Stand up now
items.explanation: 「お降りの方は、ボタンを押してください」 asks passengers getting off to press the button. Telling the driver, paying, or standing up are not mentioned.

items.stem: What time is the meeting now?
choices: 12:00 noon
items.explanation: 「午前十時から午後二時に変わりました」: the meeting moved from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. 10 a.m. is the old time; noon and 3 p.m. are not mentioned.

items.stem: Where will the meeting be held?
choices: On the second floor
In a meeting room on the third floor
At a restaurant
In Mr. Tanaka's office
items.explanation: 「場所は同じ、三階の会議室です」: the place has not changed; it is the third-floor meeting room.

items.stem: What is this message about?
choices: A dental appointment
A hair salon booking
A restaurant reservation
A package delivery
items.explanation: The caller is from 山本歯科 (Yamamoto Dental) and confirms 「ご予約」, an appointment. Nothing concerns a salon, restaurant, or delivery.

items.stem: When is the appointment?
choices: March 15, 11:00 a.m.
March 5, 1:00 p.m.
March 5, 11:00 a.m.
items.explanation: 「三月五日、金曜日の午前十一時」 is Friday, March 5 at 11 a.m. The other choices change the day (15th), the month (May), or the time (1 p.m.).

items.stem: What is the announcement mainly about?
choices: A water pipe that burst in town today
Tap water that is unsafe to drink this week
Garbage collection cancelled for tomorrow morning
No water tomorrow morning due to pipe work
items.explanation: 「水道工事のため、午前九時から正午まで水が出ません」: water will be off tomorrow from 9 to noon for waterworks. Nothing says a pipe burst, the water is unsafe, or garbage collection changes.

items.stem: What are residents asked to do?
choices: Boil their tap water
Prepare drinking water today
Stay home until noon
Report leaks to the city
items.explanation: 「飲み水は、今日のうちにご用意ください」 asks residents to get drinking water ready today. Boiling water, staying home, or reporting leaks are not requested.

items.stem: Until what time will the water be off?
choices: Noon
The evening
items.explanation: 「午前九時から正午まで」: from 9 a.m. until noon (正午). 9 a.m. is when it starts.

items.stem: Where will lunch be served today?
